scope_note: Read OWNER.md, state/briefs/example-improve.md, state/briefs/context-75.md, kb/ceremonies/75-ask-review.json, examples/ask/ in full (README.md, run.py, doors.py, harnesses.py, test.sh, admission.json, producers.json, provenance.json, entries/*.json), plus harness/policy/{interface.py,bundle.json,adapters/dryrun.py,adapters/second.py}, harness/identity/{interface.py,trust.json} for the declared scope vocabulary, and kb/research/litmus-c.jsonl for the X-litmus-c-001 wording. docs/night/hidden/ was not read and not run. Files touched: examples/ask/{README.md,run.py,doors.py,test.sh,admission.json,provenance.json} and kb/ceremonies/75-ask-improve.json. examples/ask/out/ is gitignored and regenerated by test.sh. applied.change: policy.action was carried into the decision and decided nothing, because no rule in the pinned rule set read the action path. It is now the half of a closed vocabulary that is evaluated: admission.json declares policy.actions_permitted (['submit']) beside policy.action, and run.py's new Admission.action_vocabulary() composes one deny rule - deny-entry-action-outside-vocabulary, decision_point admission.entry, one `ne` condition per permitted action, so an unregistered action matches them all - in front of the harness rule set, hands the composed bundle to the adapter's constructor and pins every decision to that bundle's own digest (self.policy.active_version) rather than to the harness bundle's. The rule set under harness/policy is untouched: composition goes through the interface's published activate(), and both bindings compile the rule because `action` is in the declared entity model. test.sh step 7 now runs the same door three ways: submit allows with allow-entry-in-tenant; action 'delete-everything' is refused 403 deny-entry-action-outside-vocabulary with spend_delta_micros 0, 0 entries, under a pin that has not moved; and the same action allows once actions_permitted names it, with the pin moving because the vocabulary is part of the digest. README section 4's decision row and a new section 6 extension row say so.

Two rungs for chains of up to four hops meant level() clamped with min(index, len-1) and hops past rung 2 held the same scope, while the record kept only the last credential's scope, so per-hop narrowing was asserted and nowhere observable. Three changes: (1) admission.json declares one rung per admissible hop - ['read:incident','read:memory','call:model','write:ledger'], four rungs against max_delegation_depth 4 and the four hop_lifetime_s rungs, every token from the identity harness's own declared scope vocabulary in trust.json rather than invented here; (2) run.py refuses instead of clamping - a chain longer than min(len(scopes), len(lifetimes)) is refused 403 policy-denied with rule_id scope-ladder-shorter-than-chain before any credential is issued, and level() is now a plain suffix with no min(); (3) the identity record carries `issued`, one entry per hop with the actor, the scope and the lifetime it was issued and the seconds left on it, plus `ladder_rungs`; issued_hops stays as the names, derived from `issued` in one expression. test.sh step 6 replaces the human-door-against-external-door comparison with a within-chain assertion at all four doors (each hop's scope a strict subset of the hop before it, lifetime and seconds_left strictly decreasing, the first hop holding exactly the declared ladder and the record's own scope equal to the last hop's), and adds the differential: four rungs issue three distinct hops on the external door, two rungs refuse the same chain with nothing recorded. Step 9 additionally asserts the detached binding's fourth hop is issued the fourth rung (600s, one scope) rather than a repeat of the third, so the deepest rung is reached by a run.

Added the missing claimed row for gap 2, in the wording the review's fix names: registry agreement is now the ninth claimed row, so every one of the nine gaps the README lists has a row under provenance.claimed and the one thing this area cannot support about its own typed refusals sits under claimed rather than nowhere.

correlation depth and parent_correlation_id were literals keyed on the format string ('a2a-message'), read at no point of decision and named in no check. admission.json now declares parent_correlation_fields ({'a2a-message': 'contextId'}); doors.parent_correlation() reads it, and depth follows from having a parent (1) or not (0) rather than from which door was used - the format literal is gone from normalise(). The record carries correlation_depth so the value is observable outside the whole-envelope comparison against a document the same author wrote. test.sh step 2 adds the differential: with contextId named, the external entry carries the partner's context as parent at depth 1 and this run's own correlation id is not the partner's; with the row removed, the same message has no parent and depth 0 and the correlation id is unchanged. A section 6 extension row names it.

The 'Carried and not consumed' row claimed every dropped member was named there and was true in one direction only: cwd, tty, datacontenttype and priority were dropped by the run and named nowhere. The row now names all of them, and the sentence is no longer taken on trust - test.sh step 2 reads the dropped lists back out of the four receipts (they are computed by doors.dropped_by) and fails if any member is not named in README.md. A member that starts being dropped now fails the visible check in the same change.

The product-name scan is now as wide as the house rule it is labelled with: word-anchored patterns (so the three-letter engine name no longer needs a trailing space to avoid 'opaque'), 25 names instead of 17 - cedar, firecracker, gvisor, jaeger, datadog, langchain, bedrock and opentelemetry added - every file of the directory walked except README.md, which is the one place a product may be named, and a floor of 12 files so a shrinking scan is visible rather than silently green. test.sh scans itself: each pattern brackets one of its own letters (r'\bopen[a]i\b'), so the literal name is not in the scanner while the pattern still matches it. The run prints 'product_hits=0 over 12 files, this scanner among them', and the 12 and the 25 in provenance are read back out of the run and counted off the pattern tuple.

notes: Every review finding id appears exactly once above: 6 applied, 2 declined.

The visible check went 55 -> 63 checks; eight were added and none removed (two for the action vocabulary plus its assertion, three for the scope ladder - the within-chain assertion replacing the two-door comparison, the short-ladder run and its assertion - two for the parent-correlation differential, one for the dropped-list-to-README direction). FLOOR in test.sh, provenance.visible_checks_counted and the printed count all read 63.

Behaviour a later reader would be surprised by: an outside check that invokes examples/ask with its own admission declaration must now declare at least one identity.scopes rung per hop the chain presents. A two-rung ladder that used to be clamped and admitted is refused 403 scope-ladder-shorter-than-chain, and the deriving binding's external door presents three hops, the detached binding's four.

Second behaviour change: policy_version is now the digest of the composed bundle (harness rule set plus this decision point's action vocabulary), not the digest of harness/policy/bundle.json. A check that computes the pin as digest_of(load_bundle()) will no longer match the one on the record.

Third: the identity record's shape grew - `issued` (per-hop actor, scope, lifetime_s, seconds_left) and `ladder_rungs` are new, and the ledger record carries correlation_depth. issued_hops is unchanged and still the list of names.

The scope rungs are the identity harness's own declared vocabulary (harness/identity/trust.json scope_vocabulary), not names invented for this example: a rung outside it is refused 422 by the interface, which is how the first four-rung ladder was caught.

The action vocabulary is composed into the pinned bundle by the example rather than added to harness/policy/bundle.json, because the improve brief permits touching only examples/ask/. Composition uses the interface's published activate() through the adapter constructor, and both bindings compile the rule (`action` is in the bundle's declared entity model), so the two-engines-one-answer differential still holds. If the vocabulary belongs in the shared rule set instead, that is a rule-set change for whoever owns harness/policy.

Not attempted, and left for the area's own gap list: nothing here reconciles the four capability-local problem-type registries with the platform's ten-row closed registry (gap 2, now under claimed). The mechanism to make that measurable does not exist in this tree - no capability publishes its registry through an interface a caller can read - so it is written as a gap with a research query rather than invented.
